key_insight: A cμ priority rule using resource-aware effective service rates is optimal in a fluid model of memory-constrained LLM inference scheduling.
engineering_relevance: LLM serving schedulers can reduce latency by prioritizing requests using holding-cost weights and effective service rates that account for compute speed, memory bandwidth, and KV-cache capacity.
method: Reduce stochastic prefill and decode workloads to a multiclass single-server fluid queue.
Prove cμ optimality for cumulative holding cost, plus completion time and full-run output-token throughput for finite workloads.
Construct a feasible finite-system policy whose scaled dynamics converge to the optimal fluid policy.
evidence_signal: Experiments on a real LLM serving engine with an NVIDIA H800 report substantially lower average latency while maintaining high throughput relative to existing scheduling policies; the abstract gives no numerical results.
watch_item: Optimality is established in the fluid limit, so finite-system performance depends on implementation details and how accurately effective service rates capture resource bottlenecks.
paper_title: Asymptotic Optimality of $cμ$-Rule for LLM Inference Scheduling under Memory Constraint
